Full read finds no calendar date in the served text itself, but overwhelming internal evidence places it in late April 2002: its own pre-match recap chain runs Extreme Beating II (31 March 2002, already dated in this registry) through Distortion 3 (23 April 2002, already dated) in strict chronological order with no gap after; commentary promotes an UPCOMING "May" PPV ("Breakaway... May __nd") as not-yet-happened; its own Lone Star/Stephon Michowski/Hardcore Scotty triple threat is fought for the International Championship's #1 contendership, fulfilled six days later when Lone Star wins the vacant title at Panic, 3 May 2002 (faw-international-r007, already dated); its own "New School" debut (Shawn Herrera, Kyle Kilbane) predates that unit's own already-dated FAW Tag Team Championship win, 2 June 2002 (faw-tag-team-r001); and, decisively, commentary calls this "an emotional week for all of FAW's wrestlers after Soulja['s] death" -- Soulja Smallz's own real-world death is independently dated to April 2002 by PTC's own news announcement (24 April 2002; see soulja-smallz's own registry row). All five threads triangulate on the same eight-or-so-day window. The exact day is not recoverable from the read corpus; month precision is as far as the evidence honestly supports. JLC's reign (faw-world-heavyweight-r023) is closed here with an inferred date (month precision, no later than this show); no new champion is crowned on this broadcast -- the closing triple threat (Vigilante/Xander/9th Wonder of Foam) is not billed as a title match, and ends with Xander attacking the winner rather than any coronation.

The FAW Hardcore Championship: this show bills and treats Neo as reigning champion, defending against Prodigy and retaining. This directly contradicts this crawl's own ledger, which has Spawn winning the title in an eight-man Hardcore battle royal at Diabolical Day (21 July 2002) with no reign closed since. No show read anywhere in this crawl documents a Spawn-to-Neo transaction in between. Recorded as read, with the contradiction noted on Spawn's own reign (faw-hardcore-r024) rather than silently resolved --  flagged for whoever next reads an intervening show that might close the gap.

A masked man ("The Real Prodigy", aka Scott Costella per the show's own closing rankings list) confronts the storyline Prodigy backstage speaking Polish, claiming to be the genuine article, then interferes on Neo's behalf in the Hardcore Championship match -- a new mystery-impostor thread, minted but not chased further this batch. Prodigy's own backstage segment (calling the interviewer "Betty", not recognizing Chris Thunder, then snapping to "Phase one... complete") reads as a brainwashing/imposter angle tied to the same thread.

Courtney "Charisma" Carter's own departure from FAW, teased by her SummerSlaughter turn, is confirmed here -- her dressing room is cleared at her own request per Tom The Bomb, and Chris Thunder drops the World Title belt in front of Tom in protest. Her tenure's last_seen is tightened to 2002-08 accordingly.

A debuting Bayne straps debuting Minion into a straitjacket and puts him through a table with the Death From Above; Muzzler then Muzzler Bombs Bayne, who kicks out, before a bleeding Minion mistakenly chairs Muzzler instead of Bayne and collapses. Bayne covers Minion for the pin and the vacant title. The text calls Muzzler "The International Champion" once mid-match, apparently in error -- he holds no title in the surviving record at this point, and every surrounding line frames this as a Hardcore Championship match.

Max X leaves the match immediately to join his girlfriend Amy at ringside and never wrestles. Deadman chairs both Pyro and Max X and covers, but Pyro kicks out and wins with a return chair shot. The following show's own commentary recaps this as "Pyro picked up the win over our own World Champion Deadman" -- but that same next show (FAW IS WAR, 28 May 2001) goes on to re-bill Deadman as the sitting World Champion, belt physically worn, defending it at the upcoming Breakaway, so this pass reads the recap line as merely identifying Deadman by his title rather than asserting a title change: an ordinary win over the champion, not a title match.

notes: Co-commentary is Bill Clinton and HaHaKlown, billed here as "President K" and a former three-time FAW World Champion.
